'''Elbio Rubén Dagotto''' is an [[Argentine-American|Argentinian-American]] [[theoretical physicist]] and academic. He is a distinguished professor in the department of physics and astronomy at the [[University of Tennessee system|University of Tennessee, Knoxville]], and Distinguished Scientist in the Materials Science and Technology Division at the [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]].<ref name=wee>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ornl.gov/staff-profile/elbio-r-dagotto|title=Elbio R Dagotto &#124; ORNL|website=www.ornl.gov}}</ref>

Dagotto is most known for using theoretical models and computational techniques to explore [[transition metal]] [[oxide]]s, oxide interfaces, [[High-temperature superconductivity|high-temperature superconductors]], topological materials, quantum magnets, and nanoscale systems.<ref name=rfv>{{Cite web|url=https://quantummaterials.utk.edu/affiliates-elbio-dagotto/|title=Affiliates – Elbio Dagotto &#124; Tennessee Quantum Center}}</ref> He authored the book, ''Nanoscale Phase Separation and Colossal Magnetoresistance'' which has focused on transition metal oxides, particularly [[manganese oxide]]s with the [[Colossal magnetoresistance|colossal magneto-resistance]] effect and co-edited the book, ''Multifunctional Oxide Heterostructures''.<ref name=ele/>

Dagotto held appointments as a Member of the Solid State Sciences Committee at the [[National Academy of Sciences]] and as a Divisional Editor for ''[[Physical Review Letters]]''. He is a Fellow of both the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS)<ref name=zzz>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/listing|title=Elected Fellows &#124; American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)|website=www.aaas.org}}</ref> and the [[American Physical Society]] (APS),<ref name=rrrr>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=www.aps.org}}</ref> and has also been recognized as an Outstanding Referee by the APS<ref name=www>{{Cite web|url=https://journals.aps.org/OutstandingReferees|title=Physical Review Journals – Outstanding Referees|website=journals.aps.org}}</ref> and ''[[EPL (journal)|Europhysics Letters]]'' (EPL).<ref name=qqq>{{Cite web|url=https://www.epletters.net/distinguished-referees/|title=Distinguished referees}}</ref> Furthermore, he is the recipient of the 2023 [[David Adler Lectureship Award in the Field of Materials Physics]]<ref name=david/> and recipient of the 2023 Alexander Prize of the University of Tennessee.<ref name=qpl>{{Cite web|url=https://honorsbanquet.utk.edu/2023-alexander-prize/|title=2023 Alexander Prize &#124; Honors Banquets|website=honorsbanquet.utk.edu}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Dagotto studied physics at the [[Balseiro Institute|Institute Balseiro]], [[Bariloche Atomic Centre]], [[Bariloche]], [[Argentina]], where he received the title of [[Licentiate (degree)|Licenciado]]. Continuing in the Centro Atomico Bariloche, he received his PhD in the field of [[Particle physics|High Energy Physics]], specifically in [[Lattice gauge theory|lattice gauge theories]]. He then moved as [[postdoctoral researcher]] to the department of physics, [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] under the supervision of [[Eduardo Fradkin]] and [[John Kogut]]. His second postdoctoral appointment was at the [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics]], at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]], where he collaborated with [[Douglas James Scalapino]], [[John Robert Schrieffer]] and Robert Sugar.<ref name=rfv/>

Dagotto became assistant, associate and then full professor at the department of physics, [[Florida State University]]. There, he was associated with the [[National High Magnetic Field Laboratory]], working in the theory group. He works in a Correlated Electron Group with [[Adriana Moreo]],<ref name=ele>{{Cite web|url=http://sces.phys.utk.edu/|title=Dagotto Group Homepage|website=sces.phys.utk.edu}}</ref> and has had a joint appointment between the University of Tennessee (UT), Knoxville, and Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) since 2004.<ref name=dkl>{{Cite web|url=http://www.phys.utk.edu/news/2022/elbio-dagotto-receives-aps-adler-award-in-materials-physics.html|title=Department of Physics and Astronomy &#124; The University of Tennessee, Knoxville|website=www.phys.utk.edu}}</ref>

==Research==
Dagotto's research has primarily focused on [[Strongly correlated material|strongly correlated electronic materials]], and lately in [[quantum materials]], where correlation and topological effects are intertwined. In the presence of strong correlation, the interactions between electrons play a crucial role and the [[Independent electron approximation|one-electron approximation]], used for example in semiconductors, is no longer valid. In this framework, he has worked on theories for many families of materials, such as [[High-temperature superconductivity|high critical temperature superconductors]] and manganese oxides with the [[colossal magnetoresistance]]. The overarching theme of his work is that correlated electrons must be considered in the broader context of complexity.<ref name="auto1">{{cite journal |last1=Dagotto |first1=Elbio |title=Complexity in Strongly Correlated Electronic Systems |journal=Science |date=8 July 2005 |volume=309 |issue=5732 |pages=257–262 |doi=10.1126/science.1107559 |pmid=16002608 |arxiv=cond-mat/0509041 |bibcode=2005Sci...309..257D }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> As described by [[Philip W. Anderson]] in his publication, "More Is Different"<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Anderson |first1=P. W. |title=More Is Different: Broken symmetry and the nature of the hierarchical structure of science. |journal=Science |date=4 August 1972 |volume=177 |issue=4047 |pages=393–396 |doi=10.1126/science.177.4047.393 |pmid=17796623 }}</ref> having simple fundamental interactions among particles does not imply the ability to reconstruct their collective properties. Dagotto argued that in correlated electronic systems, similar [[emergence]] occurs, and these complex systems spontaneously form complicated states and self-organize in patterns impossible to predict by mere inspection of the simple electron-electron interactions involved. Because of its intrinsic difficulty, to study complexity and emergence in quantum materials the use of computational techniques is crucial. He has employed [[Monte Carlo method|Monte Carlo]], [[density matrix renormalization group]], and [[Lanczos algorithm|Lanczos]] methods.<ref name="auto">{{cite journal |last1=Dagotto |first1=Elbio |title=Correlated electrons in high-temperature superconductors |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |date=July 1994 |volume=66 |issue=3 |pages=763–840 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.66.763 |arxiv=cond-mat/9311013 |bibcode=1994RvMP...66..763D }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> Together with collaborators, he also developed new algorithms to study systems described by spin-fermion models, with a mixture of quantum and classical degrees of freedom, such as in the [[Double-exchange mechanism|double exchange]] context used for materials in the central part of the ''3d'' row of the [[periodic table]].<ref name=fif>{{cite journal |last1=Dagotto |first1=Elbio |last2=Hotta |first2=Takashi |last3=Moreo |first3=Adriana |title=Colossal magnetoresistant materials: the key role of phase separation |journal=Physics Reports |date=April 2001 |volume=344 |issue=1–3 |pages=1–153 |doi=10.1016/S0370-1573(00)00121-6 |arxiv=cond-mat/0012117 |bibcode=2001PhR...344....1D }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref>

==Scientific work==
In 1992, Dagotto, in collaboration with José Riera and Doug Scalapino, opened the field of ladder compounds,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dagotto |first1=E. |last2=Riera |first2=J. |last3=Scalapino |first3=D. |title=Superconductivity in ladders and coupled planes |journal=Physical Review B |date=March 1992 |volume=45 |issue=10 |pages=5744–5747 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.45.5744 |pmid=10000307 |bibcode=1992PhRvB..45.5744D }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> materials with atomic substructures containing two chains next to each other and with inter-ladder coupling (along rungs) of magnitude comparable to that in the long direction (along legs). This research was the first to demonstrate that the transition from one chain to a full two-dimensional plane was not a smooth process simply involving the addition of one chain to another. Instead, it was revealed that even and odd number of chains (called legs due to its ladder-like geometry) belong to classes with quite different behavior.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dagotto |first1=Elbio |last2=Rice |first2=T. M. |title=Surprises on the Way from One- to Two-Dimensional Quantum Magnets: The Ladder Materials |journal=Science |date=2 February 1996 |volume=271 |issue=5249 |pages=618–623 |doi=10.1126/science.271.5249.618 |arxiv=cond-mat/9509181 |bibcode=1996Sci...271..618D }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> The even-leg ladders, with two legs being the most dramatic case, were theoretically predicted by Dagotto to display a spin gap, spin liquid properties, and tendencies toward superconductivity upon hole doping, all properties confirmed experimentally in materials of the family of copper-based high critical superconductors.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dagotto |first1=Elbio |title=Experiments on ladders reveal a complex interplay between a spin-gapped normal state and superconductivity |journal=Reports on Progress in Physics |date=November 1999 |volume=62 |issue=11 |pages=1525–1571 |doi=10.1088/0034-4885/62/11/202 |arxiv=cond-mat/9908250 |bibcode=1999RPPh...62.1525D }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> Even in the more recently discovered [[Iron-based superconductor|iron-based high critical temperature superconductor]], the "123" materials such as BaFe2S3 with ladder geometry also display superconductivity under high pressure.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Takahashi |first1=Hiroki |last2=Sugimoto |first2=Akira |last3=Nambu |first3=Yusuke |last4=Yamauchi |first4=Touru |last5=Hirata |first5=Yasuyuki |last6=Kawakami |first6=Takateru |last7=Avdeev |first7=Maxim |last8=Matsubayashi |first8=Kazuyuki |last9=Du |first9=Fei |last10=Kawashima |first10=Chizuru |last11=Soeda |first11=Hideto |last12=Nakano |first12=Satoshi |last13=Uwatoko |first13=Yoshiya |last14=Ueda |first14=Yutaka |last15=Sato |first15=Taku J. |last16=Ohgushi |first16=Kenya |title=Pressure-induced superconductivity in the iron-based ladder material BaFe2S3 |journal=Nature Materials |date=October 2015 |volume=14 |issue=10 |pages=1008–1012 |doi=10.1038/nmat4351 |pmid=26191659 |arxiv=1507.05864 }}</ref>

Dagotto employed computational techniques to study model Hamiltonians for high critical temperature superconductors based on copper,<ref name=auto/> thus reducing the uncertainty in the analysis of these models when employing other approximations, such as mean field or variational methods. In 1990, he along with research collaborators, and other groups independently, realized that the dominant attractive channel for Cooper pairs of holes in an antiferromagnetic background is the d<sub>x2-y2</sub> channel.<ref name=tthree>{{cite journal |last1=Dagotto |first1=Elbio |last2=Riera |first2=Jose |last3=Young |first3=A. P. |title=Dynamical pair susceptibilities in the t - J and Hubbard models |journal=Physical Review B |date=August 1990 |volume=42 |issue=4 |pages=2347–2352 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.42.2347 |pmid=9995682 |bibcode=1990PhRvB..42.2347D }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> In 1990, he studied dynamical properties of the [[Hubbard model]] and [[t-J model]] computationally, addressing photoemission dispersions and [[quasiparticle]] weights.<ref name=auto/><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sorella |first1=S. |last2=Martins |first2=G. B. |last3=Becca |first3=F. |last4=Gazza |first4=C. |last5=Capriotti |first5=L. |last6=Parola |first6=A. |last7=Dagotto |first7=E. |title=Superconductivity in the Two-Dimensional t − J Model |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=28 February 2002 |volume=88 |issue=11 |article-number=117002 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.88.117002 |pmid=11909422 |arxiv=cond-mat/0110460 |bibcode=2002PhRvL..88k7002S }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref>

In 1998, Dagotto developed the Monte Carlo techniques that allowed for the first computational studies of spin-fermion models for manganites, in collaboration with Seiji Yunoki and Adriana Moreo. Employing these techniques, [[phase separation]] involving electronic degrees of freedom, dubbed "electronic phase separation" was discovered.<ref name=fif/> The computational techniques developed by him and research collaborators unveiled the strong competition between a ferromagnetic metallic state and complex charge-orbital-spin ordered insulating states, providing the explanation for the colossal magnetoresistance effect in manganites.<ref name=twentyfive>{{cite journal |last1=Burgy |first1=J. |last2=Mayr |first2=M. |last3=Martin-Mayor |first3=V. |last4=Moreo |first4=A. |last5=Dagotto |first5=E. |title=Colossal Effects in Transition Metal Oxides Caused by Intrinsic Inhomogeneities |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=13 December 2001 |volume=87 |issue=27 |article-number=277202 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.87.277202 |pmid=11800911 |arxiv=cond-mat/0107300 |bibcode=2001PhRvL..87A7202B }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hotta |first1=Takashi |last2=Feiguin |first2=Adrian |last3=Dagotto |first3=Elbio |title=Stripes Induced by Orbital Ordering in Layered Manganites |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=21 May 2001 |volume=86 |issue=21 |pages=4922–4925 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.86.4922 |pmid=11384382 |arxiv=cond-mat/0012098 |bibcode=2001PhRvL..86.4922H }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref><ref name=ert>{{cite journal |last1=Şen |first1=Cengiz |last2=Alvarez |first2=Gonzalo |last3=Dagotto |first3=Elbio |title=Competing Ferromagnetic and Charge-Ordered States in Models for Manganites: The Origin of the Colossal Magnetoresistance Effect |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=21 March 2007 |volume=98 |issue=12 |article-number=127202 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.98.127202 |arxiv=cond-mat/0702426 |bibcode=2007PhRvL..98l7202S }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> More recently, similar Monte Carlo techniques have been employed by him and collaborators to study properties of iron-based superconductors, revealing the role of the lattice to stabilize the electronic nematic regime above the antiferromagnetic critical temperature.<ref name=twentytwo>{{cite journal |last1=Liang |first1=Shuhua |last2=Moreo |first2=Adriana |last3=Dagotto |first3=Elbio |title=Nematic State of Pnictides Stabilized by Interplay between Spin, Orbital, and Lattice Degrees of Freedom |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=24 July 2013 |volume=111 |issue=4 |article-number=047004 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.111.047004 |pmid=23931398 |arxiv=1305.1879 |bibcode=2013PhRvL.111d7004L }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref>

In a highly cited 2005 publication, Dagotto argued that the electronic degree of freedom in transition metal oxides and related materials displays characteristics similar to those of [[soft matter]], where complex patterns arise from deceptively simple interactions.<ref name="auto1"/>

In 2006, Dagotto and Ivan Sergienko developed a theory to understand the [[Multiferroics|multiferroic]] properties of narrow bandwidth perovskites and other oxides. Their spin arrangements break inversion symmetry, and this triggers ferroelectric properties, leading to multiferroics, which are materials with both magnetic and ferroelectric properties.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sergienko |first1=I. A. |last2=Dagotto |first2=E. |title=Role of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction in multiferroic perovskites |journal=Physical Review B |date=23 March 2006 |volume=73 |issue=9 |article-number=094434 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.73.094434 |arxiv=cond-mat/0508075 |bibcode=2006PhRvB..73i4434S }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> He, along with Ivan Sergienko, Cengiz Sen, [[Silvia Picozzi]] and collaborators also proposed magnetostriction as a mechanism for multiferroicity.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sergienko |first1=Ivan A. |last2=Şen |first2=Cengiz |last3=Dagotto |first3=Elbio |title=Ferroelectricity in the Magnetic E -Phase of Orthorhombic Perovskites |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=30 November 2006 |volume=97 |issue=22 |article-number=227204 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.97.227204 |pmid=17155837 |arxiv=cond-mat/0608025 |bibcode=2006PhRvL..97v7204S }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Picozzi |first1=S. |last2=Yamauchi |first2=K. |last3=Sanyal |first3=B. |last4=Sergienko |first4=I. A. |last5=Dagotto |first5=E. |title=Dual Nature of Improper Ferroelectricity in a Magnetoelectric Multiferroic |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=26 November 2007 |volume=99 |issue=22 |article-number=227201 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.99.227201 |pmid=18233318 |arxiv=0704.3578 |bibcode=2007PhRvL..99v7201P }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref>

Dagotto made several other contributions to theoretical [[condensed matter physics]]. Together with [[Pengcheng Dai]] and Jiangping Hu, in 2012 they were among the first to argue that the iron based high critical temperature superconductors are not located in the weak Hubbard coupling limit. Instead they are in the intermediate Hubbard coupling regime, thus requiring a combination of localized and itinerant degrees of freedom.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dai |first1=Pengcheng |last2=Hu |first2=Jiangping |last3=Dagotto |first3=Elbio |title=Magnetism and its microscopic origin in iron-based high-temperature superconductors |journal=Nature Physics |date=October 2012 |volume=8 |issue=10 |pages=709–718 |doi=10.1038/nphys2438 |arxiv=1209.0381 |bibcode=2012NatPh...8..709D }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> In particular, iron selenides are an example of materials where electronic correlations and spin frustration cannot be ignored.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dagotto |first1=Elbio |title=Colloquium: The unexpected properties of alkali metal iron selenide superconductors |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |date=20 May 2013 |volume=85 |issue=2 |pages=849–867 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.85.849 |arxiv=1210.6501 |bibcode=2013RvMP...85..849D }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> With Julian Rincon, Jacek Herbrych and collaborators,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Herbrych |first1=J. |last2=Heverhagen |first2=J. |last3=Patel |first3=N. D. |last4=Alvarez |first4=G. |last5=Daghofer |first5=M. |last6=Moreo |first6=A. |last7=Dagotto |first7=E. |title=Novel Magnetic Block States in Low-Dimensional Iron-Based Superconductors |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=10 July 2019 |volume=123 |issue=2 |article-number=027203 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.123.027203 |pmid=31386537 |arxiv=1812.00325 |bibcode=2019PhRvL.123b7203H }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Patel |first1=N. D. |last2=Nocera |first2=A. |last3=Alvarez |first3=G. |last4=Moreo |first4=A. |last5=Johnston |first5=S. |last6=Dagotto |first6=E. |title=Fingerprints of an orbital-selective Mott phase in the block magnetic state of BaFe2Se3 ladders |journal=Communications Physics |date=21 June 2019 |volume=2 |issue=1 |article-number=64 |doi=10.1038/s42005-019-0155-3 |doi-access=free|arxiv=1807.10419 }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> employing the density matrix renormalization group, they computationally discovered "block" states in low-dimensional multi-orbital Hubbard models. Spin blocks are groups of spin that are aligned ferromagnetically, anti-ferro coupled among them, and they display exotic dynamical spin structure factors with a mixture of spin waves and optical modes.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Spin dynamics of the block orbital-selective Mott phase|journal=Nature Communications |date=19 May 2021 |volume=12 |issue=1 |page=2955 |doi=10.1038/s41467-021-23261-2  |doi-access=free|last1=Herbrych |first1=J. |last2=Środa |first2=M. |last3=Alvarez |first3=G. |last4=Mierzejewski |first4=M. |last5=Dagotto |first5=E. |pmid=34011947 |pmc=8134496 |arxiv=2011.05646 |bibcode=2021NatCo..12.2955H }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref>

Among the related findings, Herbrych, Dagotto and collaborators revealed the existence of a spin spiral made out of blocks, a state never reported before.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Block–spiral magnetism: An exotic type of frustrated order|first1=J.|last1=Herbrych|first2=J.|last2=Heverhagen|first3=G.|last3=Alvarez|first4=M.|last4=Daghofer|first5=A.|last5=Moreo|first6=E.|last6=Dagotto|date=July 14, 2020|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|volume=117|issue=28|pages=16226–16233|doi=10.1073/pnas.2001141117|pmid=32601231|pmc=7368323 |arxiv=1911.12248 |bibcode=2020PNAS..11716226H |doi-access=free }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> When this spiral one-dimensional state is placed over a two-dimensional superconducting plane, [[Majorana fermion]]s developed at the chain by proximity effect from the plane,<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Interaction-induced topological phase transition and Majorana edge states in low-dimensional orbital-selective Mott insulators|first1=J.|last1=Herbrych|first2=M.|last2=Środa|first3=G.|last3=Alvarez|first4=M.|last4=Mierzejewski|first5=E.|last5=Dagotto|date=May 19, 2021|journal=Nature Communications|volume=12|issue=1|page=2955|doi=10.1038/s41467-021-23261-2|doi-access=free|pmid=34011947 |pmc=8134496 |arxiv=2011.05646 |bibcode=2021NatCo..12.2955H }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> and for this reason this chain-plane geometry has potential value in [[Topological quantum computer|topological quantum computing]]. He, together with Narayan Mohanta and Satoshi Okamoto, also reported Majoranas in a two-dimensional three-layer geometry with a skyrmion crystal at the bottom, an electron gas in the middle, and a standard superconductor at the top with a carved one-dimensional channel.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mohanta |first1=Narayan |last2=Okamoto |first2=Satoshi |last3=Dagotto |first3=Elbio |title=Skyrmion control of Majorana states in planar Josephson junctions |journal=Communications Physics |date=15 July 2021 |volume=4 |issue=1 |article-number=163 |doi=10.1038/s42005-021-00666-5 |doi-access=free|bibcode=2021CmPhy...4..163M |arxiv=2012.13502 }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> Within topology in one dimension, he, Nirav Patel, and collaborators proposed a fermionic two-orbital electronic model that becomes the S=1 Haldane chain in strong Hubbard coupling,<ref name=qaz>{{cite journal |last1=Patel |first1=Niravkumar D. |last2=Kaushal |first2=Nitin |last3=Nocera |first3=Alberto |last4=Alvarez |first4=Gonzalo |last5=Dagotto |first5=Elbio |title=Emergence of superconductivity in doped multiorbital Hubbard chains |journal=npj Quantum Materials |date=8 May 2020 |volume=5 |issue=1 |article-number=27 |doi=10.1038/s41535-020-0228-2 |doi-access=free|arxiv=2001.00589 |bibcode=2020npjQM...5...27P }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> and has similarities with the [[AKLT model|AKLT state]] of spin systems. The proposed fermionic model has a spin gap and spin liquid properties, as the Haldane chain, and it is quite different from the S=1/2 Heisenberg chain. Moreover, he and collaborators predicted superconductivity upon hole doping, similarly as it occurs in ladders due to the existence of preformed spin ½ singlets in the ground state as in a [[Resonating valence bond theory|resonant valence bond state]].<ref name=qaz/>

Dagotto also contributed to theoretical aspects of oxide interfaces, where oxides are grown one over the other creating interfaces where reconstructions of the spin, charge, orbital, and lattice can occur.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dagotto |first1=Elbio |title=When Oxides Meet Face to Face |journal=Science |date=16 November 2007 |volume=318 |issue=5853 |pages=1076–1077 |doi=10.1126/science.1151094 |pmid=18006728 }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> Together with Shuai Dong and collaborators, he showed that a superlattice made of insulating Mn-oxide components becomes globally metallic in the new geometry.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dong |first1=Shuai |last2=Yu |first2=Rong |last3=Yunoki |first3=Seiji |last4=Alvarez |first4=Gonzalo |last5=Liu |first5=J.-M. |last6=Dagotto |first6=Elbio |title=Magnetism, conductivity, and orbital order in (LaMnO{{sub|3}}){{sub|2''n''}} / (SrMnO{{sub|3}}){{sub|''n''}} superlattices |journal=Physical Review B |date=21 November 2008 |volume=78 |issue=20 |article-number=201102 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.78.201102 |arxiv=0810.1441 }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> He has also worked in skyrmions.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mohanta |first1=Narayan |last2=Christianson |first2=Andrew D. |last3=Okamoto |first3=Satoshi |last4=Dagotto |first4=Elbio |title=Signatures of a liquid-crystal transition in spin-wave excitations of skyrmions |journal=Communications Physics |date=11 December 2020 |volume=3 |issue=1 |article-number=229 |doi=10.1038/s42005-020-00489-w |doi-access=free|arxiv=2005.11399 |bibcode=2020CmPhy...3..229M }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> In the early stages of his career, he made contributions: to particle physics<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kogut |first1=J. B. |last2=Dagotto |first2=Elbio |last3=Kocic |first3=A. |title=New phase of quantum electrodynamics: A nonperturbative fixed point in four dimensions |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=29 February 1988 |volume=60 |issue=9 |pages=772–775 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.60.772 |pmid=10038648 |bibcode=1988PhRvL..60..772K }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> in the context of lattice gauge theories, to the interface between particle physics and condensed matter,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fradkin |first1=Eduardo |last2=Dagotto |first2=Elbio |last3=Boyanovsky |first3=Daniel |title=Physical Realization of the Parity Anomaly in Condensed Matter Physics |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=8 December 1986 |volume=57 |issue=23 |pages=2967–2970 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.57.2967 |pmid=10033920 |bibcode=1986PhRvL..57.2967F }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dagotto |first1=Elbio |last2=Fradkin |first2=Eduardo |last3=Moreo |first3=Adriana |title=SU(2) gauge invariance and order parameters in strongly coupled electronic systems |journal=Physical Review B |date=August 1988 |volume=38 |issue=4 |pages=2926–2929 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.38.2926 |pmid=9946627 |bibcode=1988PhRvB..38.2926D }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref> and to frustrated spin systems.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dagotto |first1=Elbio |last2=Moreo |first2=Adriana |title=Phase diagram of the frustrated spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet in 2 dimensions |journal=Physical Review Letters |date=6 November 1989 |volume=63 |issue=19 |pages=2148–2151 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.63.2148 |pmid=10040774 |bibcode=1989PhRvL..63.2148D }}{{psc|date=September 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Dagotto is married to [[Adriana Moreo]], another physicist with whom he has two children; they met as undergraduates at the Balseiro Institute.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://trace.tennessee.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1018&context=utk-cross|title=Have Theory, Will Travel: Elbio Dagotto and Adriana Moreo Bring a Top-Flight Program to UT|pages=1–2, 7|magazine=Cross Sections|volume=8|issue=2|date=Fall–Winter 2004|publisher=University of Tennessee Department of Physics & Astronomy|access-date=2023-10-05}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
*1998 – Fellow, American Physical Society<ref name=rrrr/>
*2006 – Member, Solid State Sciences Committee of the National Academy of Sciences<ref>{{cite book |title=Inspired by Biology: From Molecules to Materials to Machines |date=2008 |publisher=National Academies Press (US) |chapter-url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK214497/ |chapter=Solid State Sciences Committee }}</ref>
*2008 – Outstanding Referee, American Physical Society (APS)<ref name=www/>
*2010 – Fellow, American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)<ref name=zzz/>
*2012 – Outstanding Referee, Europhysics Letters (EPL)<ref name=qqq/>
*2019, 2021, 2023 – Teacher of the year award, University of Tennessee<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.phys.utk.edu/alumni-friends/awardees-toty.html|title=Department of Physics and Astronomy &#124; The University of Tennessee, Knoxville|website=www.phys.utk.edu}}</ref>
*2023 – David Adler Lectureship Award in the Field of Materials Physics, American Physical Society<ref name=david>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/adler.cfm|title=David Adler Lectureship Award in the Field of Materials Physics|website=www.aps.org}}</ref> with citation "For pioneering work on the theoretical framework of correlated electron systems and describing their importance through elegant written and oral communications."
*2023 – Alexander Prize, University of Tennessee<ref name=qpl/>
